responses.question: Should the "classic calculator" look target a specific physical calculator model, or just a general retro/classic aesthetic?
responses.why: Scopes the visual target and avoids blocking on pinning an exact reference model.
responses.answer: General retro/classic look; no single reference model to match.

responses.question: Should this classic-look change apply only to the app's default theme, or to all theme options?
responses.why: Bounds the blast radius of the shared CSS token changes.
responses.answer: Only the default/classic theme. Other themes (e.g. dark mode) remain unchanged.

responses.question: Should Standard mode be the primary target, or should all modes be explicitly restyled together?
responses.why: Defines the scope boundary and acceptance criteria for verification.
responses.answer: Standard mode is the primary target. Other modes (scientific, converter, financial, grapher) inherit shared styling passively via shared CSS tokens; they are not explicitly restyled as part of this change.

responses.question: What visual traits define the classic look?
responses.why: Concrete, testable visual acceptance criteria for the Standard mode redesign.
responses.answer: Raised/beveled physical-style buttons, a recessed LCD-style display panel, and a muted classic color palette (grey/beige tones) with simple borders/shadows.
